title: TSMC’s Quarterly Revenue Jumps 51% After AI Demand Holds Up
source_used: Startup Fortune (figures also confirmed by Euronews)
key_facts: TSMC said third-quarter revenue rose 51% year on year to NT$1.49 trillion.
That beat the NT$1.46 trillion analysts had expected, according to Bloomberg.
September revenue was NT$511.86 billion, up 54.6% from a year earlier, within a hair of August's all-time monthly high.
Nvidia and Apple remain TSMC's two biggest customers (Startup Fortune).
Euronews confirms the 51% quarterly rise, the 54.6% September rise and the NT$1.49 trillion total.
Euronews says the total beat the top of TSMC's own guidance.
TSMC will report full third-quarter results and its outlook on 15 October (Euronews).
quote_evidence: TSMC said on October 8 that its third-quarter revenue rose 51% year over year to NT$1.49 trillion.
September alone brought in NT$511.86 billion, up 54.6% from a year earlier.
why_it_matters_hint: AI chip demand held up in the September and quarterly sales figures; one quarter does not show how long orders last.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked (HTTP 403). Startup Fortune is readable and cites Bloomberg for the analyst estimate. Euronews gives the same 51% and NT$1.49 trillion. Dollar conversions differ (Euronews $46.8bn, Startup Fortune $48.4bn), so no dollar figure is printed. Startup Fortune is a smaller outlet; the summary uses only figures Euronews also confirms.
